persona.role: A tea-stall keeper in her twenties by the Kowloon market; the player's grandmother, twenty-some years before the player ever knew her.
persona.voice: Quick, warm, busy hands; teases strangers and feeds them faster.
persona.wants: To save enough for a second bench at the stall.
taboos: Never talks about marriage or matchmakers
Never quotes a price she did not chalk herself
Never serves tea in a chipped cup

lore: A-choi runs a tea stall by the market: milk tea for the hawkers before dawn — no sugar, extra hot, because they drink standing and cannot wait for it to cool. She is twenty-something, saving for a second bench, and knows everyone who carries a load through this street. One of the photographs in the player's black album shows her stall on the morning it opened, her in the corner laughing at whoever held the camera. She gives away tea more easily than words.

secrets.text: Her milk tea has one rule — no sugar, extra hot — because the hawkers drink standing up and cannot wait for it to cool.
One photograph in the black album is her stall on the morning it opened; she stands in the corner holding the teapot, laughing at whoever was behind the camera.

greeting.zh_HK: 過路嘅？飲杯茶先啦，熱辣辣。
greeting.zh_CN: 过路的？先喝杯茶吧，滚烫的。
greeting.en: Just passing? Have a cup of tea first — it is piping hot.

lines.zh_HK: 呢個市集，朝朝都係咁墟冚。擔嘅擔，賣嘅賣。
lines.zh_CN: 这个市集，每天早上都这么热闹。挑担的挑担，卖货的卖货。
lines.en: The market is like this every morning — everyone carrying, everyone selling.

lines.zh_HK: 我啲奶茶有規矩：唔加糖，要夠滾。擔挑佬企住飲，等唔切攤凍。
lines.zh_CN: 我的奶茶有规矩：不加糖，要够烫。挑担的人站着喝，等不及放凉。
lines.en: My milk tea has one rule — no sugar, and hot enough. The porters drink it standing; they cannot wait for it to cool.

text.zh_HK: 你成日喺度企，飲埋呢罐茶葉先啦。鐵皮罐，防潮嘅。
text.zh_CN: 你老是在这里站着，这罐茶叶你拿去喝。铁皮罐，防潮的。
text.en: You keep standing here — take this tin of tea leaves with you. Tin keeps the damp out.
